pageCache.text:
‘At Broomwood, we inspire confident, curious, and happy learners. Across our Pre-Prep, Boys’ and Girls’ sites, we combine academic excellence with a love of sport, music, and the arts, creating a vibrant and supportive community where every child can thrive. We look forward to welcoming you to our family.’
Mr Michael Hodge, Principal
Why Broomwood?
Inspiring curious, capable young learners. At Broomwood, children grow in independence, curiosity and confidence from day one. Across our Pre-Prep and Prep schools, boys and girls benefit from a distinctive educational pathway that combines co-education in the early years with single-sex learning in later stages, allowing tailored academic and pastoral support. Our curriculum balances academic ambition with creativity, sport, music, and the arts, while fostering character, resilience, and collaboration. Supported by outstanding facilities, a dedicated team of educators, and a supportive, values-led environment, Broomwood pupils are equipped not only for academic success – reflected in 39 scholarships achieved in 2025 – but for personal growth and lifelong learning. From Early Years through to Prep, our school community prioritises every child’s individual potential, preparing them confidently for the next stage of their education and beyond.
Our School
Broomwood offers an exceptional education where children thrive academically, socially, and personally. They leave as confident, well-rounded individuals, ready to take their place at top day and boarding schools, equipped not just with excellent results, but with the skills and character to flourish.
Broomwood Leavers Destinations 2025
Broomwood Leavers Successes 2025
A Tailored Approach
Children join our Pre-Prep at either age 3 in Little Broomwood or age 4 in Reception, and continue together seamlessly through to the end of Year 2. They move on to our single-sex schools, Broomwood Prep – Girls and Broomwood Prep – Boys from Year 3 (ages 7–13). While their learning is tailored to their needs, pupils continue to come together for a wide range of co-educational activities, including House events, residential trips, and workshops. This approach combines focused academic support with rich opportunities for shared experiences.
Little Broomwood
Boys & Girls aged 3-4
At Little Broomwood, we understand how important the early years are for the development of your child. Our aim is to nurture young minds, preparing children for an outstanding education in a friendly home-like environment.
Pre-Prep
Boys & Girls aged 3-7
Broomwood Pre-Prep is a vibrant, happy place, filled with the laughter of children who truly enjoy being with us. We understand how important the early years are for a child’s development, and our aim is to provide an outstanding education that nurtures young minds while equipping them with the skills and confidence they need for life.
Prep Schools
Boys aged 7-13
Broomwood Prep – Boys offers a broad and engaging education where academic excellence sits alongside co-curricular activities. Boys thrive in a supportive, energetic environment, enjoying opportunities that challenge them while fostering curiosity, confidence, and a genuine love of learning.
Girls aged 7-13
Broomwood Prep – Girls provides a forward-looking, well-rounded education in a welcoming, inspiring setting. Girls are encouraged to explore their interests, develop independence, and grow academically and personally, with a curriculum that stretches and challenges them while fostering curiosity, confidence, and creativity. All of this takes place within a supportive community that develops each child’s potential and celebrates individual achievement.
Latest News
Broomwood shortlisted for five Education Choices Magazine Awards 2026
Broomwood named Best Independent Preparatory School in London for second consecutive year
Where next?
Please take a look around our website. While this gives a glimpse of life at Broomwood, it can only show a fraction of the amazing things our pupils do every day. To experience the school fully, we warmly invite you to visit us. Visit our admissions section to book an open morning or a small-group tour.
Getting to Broomwood
We look forward to showing you around our school, click on the link below for our location.

Vision, Aims & Values
#BeYourBEST
At Broomwood, we believe that success is not simply measured through attainment and academic achievements. Pupils’ welfare, both physical and mental, underpins our approach to supporting each individual in their educational journey. Pupils thrive where they are valued, heard and respected.
At Broomwood, our aim is to incorporate a holistic approach to education, focusing on both academic and personal development within a positive, safe, and encouraging school environment. Our aims can best be separated into three areas:
Everything we do at Broomwood is driven by our core values, ensuring each child thrives, as well as making a positive impact in the wider community. Our unrelenting focus is on developing the whole child, preparing pupils to lead lives that are both happy and purposeful:
With help from Rosie O’Driscoll, who has run art workshops at Broomwood, whilst being a professional artist and professional sign writer, pupils at Broomwood Girls hand painted a fantastic Broomwood Values picture in their dining hall. Take a look below to watch seven hours work condensed into one minute!

Welcome from the Principal
We believe in your child
At Broomwood, we provide an extraordinary education, where each person is valued as an individual, enjoying a proper childhood, full of fun and adventure.
We have a unique approach: boys and girls are educated together in our co-ed Pre-Prep, before moving at the age of seven to Broomwood Boys or Broomwood Girls. They benefit from a bespoke programme but come together beyond the classroom for co-ed activities, such as academic extension, sport, creative arts and residential trips. We enjoy some of the best exam results in London, but more importantly our young people move on to senior school as well-rounded, self-confident individuals. The best of both worlds.
In our website you will see something of the huge range of opportunities our children have. We look forward to meeting you and telling you more.
Michael Hodge, Principal
“Academically ambitious, pastorally kind”

Safeguarding & Welfare
Wellbeing matters
“We want every pupil to feel safe, both in and out of school. Part of this means knowing that there is always someone you can turn to and trust.”
Each of our school sites has a designated safeguarding lead (DSL) with overall responsibility for the management of safeguarding, supported by a Deputy DSL’s. Our pastoral teams meet regularly to ensure that we have a whole child-view, and all staff are trained in dealing with safeguarding concerns.
At Broomwood, we ensure that every pupil’s wellbeing and happiness is central to all that we do and bound into our structures and processes, whether via the House and tutor systems, counselling or within regular staff meetings.
Equality and inclusivity
As a co-educational school we actively educate our pupils about diversity in all its many forms, and we encourage and promote a culture of tolerance and respect in each of our schools.
We work with our local agencies – including the Wandsworth Safeguarding Board. They are satisfied that the protocols we follow are robust and any concerns are dealt with swiftly and appropriately. The Department for Education has opened a helpline to provide support and guidance to adults and children who have experienced sexual harassment or abuse in education.
Operation Encompass
Broomwood is committed to working in partnership with the Metropolitan Police through Operation Encompass, a national initiative that supports children who may have been affected by domestic abuse.
When the police attend a domestic incident where a child is involved or part of the household, the school may receive a confidential notification before the next school day. This information is shared with the Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) at the relevant Broomwood site, who can ensure that appropriate support is available for the child and their family.
As part of our commitment to safeguarding and wellbeing, Operation Encompass helps us provide timely, sensitive support when it is needed most.
For more information, please visit www.operationencompass.org

Pre-Prep Curriculum
Building Foundations
The Pre-Prep curriculum at Broomwood has been designed to provide your child with a thorough mastery of the fundamental building blocks of education. At the same time, we want to excite our pupil’s curiosity; we want them to have fun and to take an active role in their learning. We encourage a growth mindset so that children are not afraid to take academic risks, overcome learning challenges and developing resilience.
Thematic Learning
Our curriculum is delivered through ‘thematic learning’ which encompasses all major subjects such as English, Maths, History, Geography, Science, Art and ICT. This enables children to see how the world is connected, stimulating both the left and right side of the brain, enhancing linguistic and creative capacity. It also gives them the opportunity to develop creative thinking, planning and teamworking skills.

Wraparound Care
Before and After School Care
We recognise that working parents may need a little more flexibility when it comes to school hours. That’s why we offer both before and after school care through Junior Adventures Group (JAG) – one of the UK’s leading providers of wraparound care. JAG is available until 6pm for five days a week and is run by Junior Adventures Group. This is for all year groups in the Pre-Prep and is held in the Vicarage Hall until 6pm every day. Children can also attend this care after their normal after school club. The care is tailored to each child; those who still feel energetic can let off some steam, but if a child is tired and wants a cosy place to relax, that is provided too.
Places can be booked through the JAG website.
Mornings
We have an Early Waiters club which runs from 7.30 am each morning.
Afternoons
Each of our school sites also runs a wide-ranging after school clubs programme which is separate from the wrap around care service. These clubs are booked by parents at the beginning of each term. You can find out more about After School Cubs here

Broomwood named Best Independent Preparatory School in London for second consecutive year
Posted: 29th May 2026
Broomwood, Clapham, is celebrating after being named Best Independent Preparatory School 2026 in London at the prestigious LUXlife Private Education Awards, marking the second consecutive year the school has received the accolade.
The award recognises excellence across the independent education sector and celebrates schools that are delivering outstanding academic outcomes, exceptional pastoral care and an inspiring educational experience for pupils and families.
Principal and Head of Broomwood Boys, Michael Hodge said: ‘We are absolutely delighted to receive this award for a second consecutive year. It is a wonderful recognition of the exceptional staff, pupils and families who make Broomwood such a special community.
‘At Broomwood, we are committed to providing an ambitious, nurturing and forward-thinking education where children are inspired to achieve their very best, both academically and personally. To see this recognised nationally, alongside our strongest-ever scholarship outcomes, is incredibly rewarding.’
The recognition comes at an exciting time for Broomwood, following a record-breaking year for scholarships across both Year 6 and Year 8. This year, pupils secured 47 scholarships to some of the country’s most academically selective senior schools and prestigious boarding schools, with nearly half awarded for academic achievement.
Earlier this year, Broomwood was included in Talk Education’s highly regarded Top 250 Schools list, further reinforcing the school’s growing reputation as one of London’s leading preparatory schools.
Louisa McCafferty, Head of Broomwood Girls, added: ‘This award reflects the energy, creativity and care that can be felt throughout our school every single day. We are proud to offer an environment where girls and boys are encouraged to be confident, curious and courageous learners.
‘Combined with our recent scholarship success and inclusion in Talk Education’s Top 250 Schools, it is a very exciting moment for the whole Broomwood community.’
Located in the heart of Clapham, Broomwood is known for its distinctive educational approach, combining academic excellence with outstanding pastoral care, creativity and opportunity both inside and outside the classroom.
Last month, Broomwood also announced it would be expanding its Pre-School (3+) provision to include an additional class, further strengthening its early years offering.
Broomwood also operates a bus service across London, with routes serving areas including Pimlico, Wimbledon, Battersea and Tooting Bec, making the school accessible to families across the capital.
The LUXlife Private Education Awards celebrate schools and educational organisations across the UK and internationally that are making a significant impact within the sector through innovation, achievement and excellence.

History
Coming together as ‘Broomwood’
In September 2023, Northcote Lodge, Broomwood Hall Upper School and Broomwood Hall Lower School united under one name, Broomwood.
Broomwood Hall School, a pre-preparatory school for boys and girls was founded in 1984 by Katherine and Malcolm Colquhoun. The later opening of Northcote Lodge (now Broomwood Prep – Boys) and Broomwood Upper (now Broomwood Prep – Girls) meant children could continue their “Broomwood” education.
Uniting as Broomwood, meant the schools could continue to offer an excellent education with even more collaboration across the different sites. The new logo and branding drew on the best of the existing identities combining the existing Broomwood ‘B’ with the Northcote stag.

The Timeline of Broomwood
2024 – Michael Hodge joins as Principal, Broomwood and Head of Broomwood Boys.
2023 – all three schools: Broomwood Hall Lower School, Broomwood Hall Upper School & Northcote Lodge re-brand as Broomwood.
2021 – Sir Malcolm and Lady Colquhoun, founding Principals of Northwood Schools sell the group to the Dukes Education Family of Schools and Kevin Doble joins as Principal.
Carol Jenkinson retires as Head of Broomwood Hall Upper and Lower School. She is succeeded by Louisa McCafferty (Upper School) and Caron Mackay (Lower School).
2020 – Opening of new co-educational secondary school for pupils aged 11-16 in SW16 – Head, Susan Brooks
2018 – Clive Smith Langridge joined as Headmaster of Northcote Lodge.

1993 – Northcote Lodge founded under Headmaster, Desmond Bain
1984 – Broomwood Hall School founded by Katharine Mears in the Methodist Church Hall in Broomwood Road with 12 children.

pageCache.pageTitle: Outdoor Learning in Clapham | Broomwood Pre-Prep
pageCache.text:
Outdoor Learning
Space to explore, confidence to grow.
At Broomwood Pre-Prep in Clapham, outdoor learning is part of everyday school life for children aged 3–7. Our extensive outdoor spaces are used throughout the school day, giving children opportunities to learn through movement, imaginative play and practical discovery.
With activities suited to different ages and stages, our teachers help children make connections between what they learn in the classroom through our curriculum and the world around them.
Pre-Prep
Pre-Prep Curriculum
Outdoor Learning
Little Broomwood
Little Broomwood Curriculum
Activities & Enrichment
Joining & Moving On
Outdoor spaces designed for young children
Our playgrounds are carefully planned learning environments, with space for lively exploration and quieter moments. Our children, from Nursery to Year 2, enjoy:
Taking learning beyond the classroom
Counting objects in the playground makes early maths practical and engaging. Exploring materials and textures encourages children to notice differences, ask questions and describe what they discover.
A shared recipe for a “magical potion” brings opportunities to exchange ideas, take turns and solve problems. Storytelling and role play help children practise new vocabulary and express themselves with growing confidence.
This is purposeful play, thoughtfully supported by teachers who know how to turn a child’s curiosity into a learning opportunity.
Building physical confidence and independence
As children run, climb and balance, they develop strength, coordination and confidence in their own abilities. Crossing stepping stones or trying a new piece of equipment also gives them opportunities to make decisions, assess risk and persevere.
These small challenges help children experience the satisfaction of working something out for themselves and becoming more independent, while also preparing them for Broomwood’s excellent range of extracurricular activities and sports.
Supporting wellbeing and friendships
Time outdoors gives children room to move and reset, helping them return to learning with renewed focus. Alongside active play, our quieter spaces offer somewhere to pause or enjoy a calm moment with a friend.
Shared outdoor activities also encourage children to listen to one another, cooperate and build friendships. For some children, learning through a practical activity outdoors can be a particularly effective way to engage.
Book an Open Morning
Frequently Asked Questions About Outdoor Learning
What is outdoor learning at Broomwood Pre-Prep?
Outdoor learning is a core part of the school day at Broomwood Pre-Prep, not an occasional extra. Children move their learning outside to explore, build, create and problem-solve in spaces designed for their age and stage, from the mud kitchen to the outdoor theatre. It runs alongside classroom teaching to build confidence, independence and a love of discovery.
Which age groups take part in outdoor learning?
Outdoor learning runs across Broomwood Pre-Prep for children aged 3 to 7, from Nursery through to Year 2. Activities are adapted to each stage, so younger children in Nursery and Reception enjoy sensory, imaginative play such as the mud kitchen, while Year 1 and Year 2 pupils take on more physical and cooperative challenges like balance beams and team games.
Do children go outside every day, whatever the weather?
Yes. Outdoor learning happens throughout the school day, in all but the most extreme weather. Children are dressed appropriately for the season, and wet or cold conditions often become part of the lesson itself, from splashing in puddles to talking about wind and the seasons, so learning continues outside all year round.
What outdoor facilities does Broomwood Pre-Prep have?
Our outdoor spaces include an outdoor theatre with a storytelling stage and costumes, tuff trays for sensory exploration, stepping stones and balance beams, larger play equipment, and quieter areas for reflection. Each space is designed for children aged 3 to 7, giving every child room to explore, build and play safely.
How does outdoor learning support the early years curriculum?
Outdoor learning brings the Early Years Foundation Stage and National Curriculum to life through hands-on experience. Counting objects or acting out a story outdoors builds early maths, communication, problem-solving and understanding of the world, turning everyday play into purposeful, curriculum-linked learning.
Does outdoor learning continue in Year 1 and Year 2?
Outdoor learning continues right through Broomwood Pre-Prep, adapting as children grow. In Year 1 and Year 2, activities place more emphasis on physical confidence, coordination, decision-making and teamwork, building on the imaginative and sensory play first introduced back in Nursery and Reception.
What should my child wear for outdoor learning?
We recommend comfortable, weather-appropriate clothing that can get muddy, along with wellies or suitable outdoor shoes and a waterproof coat for cooler months. Our children spend time outdoors every day, so clothes that allow free movement help them get the most from the tuff trays and active play.
How does outdoor play support my child's development?
Outdoor play supports physical, social, and emotional development. Running, climbing and balancing build strength and coordination, while shared activities like storytelling and role play encourage cooperation, communication and friendship. Time outdoors also gives children space to reset, helping them return to learning with renewed focus.
Can I see the outdoor spaces before applying?
Yes. We welcome prospective families to visit Broomwood Pre-Prep in Clapham and see our outdoor learning spaces first-hand. You can book a personal tour or attend an open event to meet our teachers, explore the mud kitchen and outdoor theatre, and watch outdoor learning in action.
Visit Us
To see our outdoor learning spaces for yourself, book a personal tour or join us at our next open event. Our admissions team would be delighted to show you around Broomwood Pre-Prep.

Parents Association
Central to the Broomwood Community
Broomwood has a very active and friendly Parents’ Association. It operates as one charity, with separate Chairs at each site. All parents are encouraged to get involved and it is a great way to get to know people across the different school sites and throughout the school.
The PA organises the social activities of the school and raises money for charity.
Monies raised are donated to a rotating ‘charity of the year’.
The PA holds events for both parents and children throughout the school year such as termly cake sales, book sales and other social activities. Past events have included parties, fêtes, sponsored reading and running competitions and an annual quiz night.
The PA also acts as the voice of the parent body and holds regular meetings with the school Heads.
The PA has a Secretary and a Treasurer, as well as the site Chairs, and is made up of a representative from each Year and form in the school. Reps attend PA meetings which are held four times during the year (twice in the Autumn term and once each in the Spring and Summer term) and help with the activities that are organised during that year.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral Care | Girls School London | Broomwood
pageCache.text:
Pastoral Care
We know the importance of creating a warm, friendly and nurturing environment. At Broomwood, we pride ourselves on offering outstanding pastoral care where each child feels valued and cared for. Our school sites are dynamic yet small and intimate enough, for all children to be well known to all our staff.
We believe that reward and praise bring out the best in every child hence we provide a whole range of different arenas such as academic tasks, music, drama, sport, competitions, and themed events in which our pupils can shine, be happy and confident.
House System
Awards & Responsibilities
House System
The house system at Broomwood encourages a sense of team spirit and belonging.
At the start of their school journey into the Pre-Prep school, children are allocated a place in one of our four Houses in which they remain throughout the years with us.
Our house system is across all sites, so that boys and girls can collaborate across a variety of competitions, activities and social events.
The houses are named after the roads that link us together: Sudbrooke, Rusham, Thurleigh, Blenkarne.
In the Pre-Prep, each house has its own lunch monitor and House Captains, a boy and a girl who are appointed termly. Houses compete with one another in various ways, with House Points awarded to teams in inter-house competitions, and to individual children for manners, tidiness and effort.
Our pupils at Broomwood Prep – Boys and Broomwood Prep – Girls remain in their respective Houses as they move up from the Pre-Prep. They also welcome new children who are allocated evenly across the houses. A House Captain and a vice-Captain are chosen from Year 8 along with a vice-Captain from Year 6 (who serves for half a term). A member of staff is appointed to act as Housemistress or Housemaster for each house. All staff have a particular allegiance to one House.
Houses continue to compete vigorously with one another in various ways through a system of House points. There are inter house matches, music competitions, quizzes and poetry contests. Regular House Assemblies are held to motivate the members to gain House points and to win the coveted House Point Cup.
With its emphasis on loyalty and togetherness, the House system is instrumental in encouraging a sense of belonging and healthy competition within the school.
Tutors
We believe it is essential that each of our pupils has someone within the Broomwood school community to support, supervise and mentor them. This is why form tutors play a significant role in our children’s experience at Broomwood.
All our children are under the supervision and care of a form tutor who oversees their academic, social and personal wellbeing. Tutors have regular individual and group meetings, both formal and informal, with their tutees. At these meetings, they discuss academic performance and extra-curricular activities, as well as any aspects of their lives both at school and at home.
Tutors play a key role in our children’s day-to-day school activities and help keep track of their progress, house-points, successes and concerns. We encourage our parents to contact their children’s tutors if they have any concerns or queries.
The tutor system adds another layer to our pastoral care provision, working hand in hand with the tutees, teachers and parents.
Awards & Responsibilities
‘We recognise and reward both talent and effort..’
At Broomwood, we want your children to feel they count, and that effort is always worthwhile, even if they find a subject challenging. We recognise positive attitude, improvement, and good manners, as well as academic excellence. We also look to reward those who excel in sport, music, drama and the creative arts. There are award assemblies each half and end of term and a leavers prize-giving service at the close of the academic year. We monitor the awards to make sure no pupil does through a year without achieving a prize or certificate for something deserved.
Throughout their time at Broomwood, our pupils are given positions of responsibility. These culminate in Year 8 with the major positions – Head Boy and Head Girl, Head of House and Prefect. Pupils also have the chance to take on additional roles such as Maths Prefect, and Vice House Captains and Deputy head of House.
Our focus is on encouragement as well as celebrating success. The aim is to build character and confidence, and to prepare our children for the future. We want them to start the next phase of their education and beyond that, with a sense of achievement and confidence.
School Council
We have a school council which aims to be the voice for the pupil body.
The School Council comprises elected representatives from Years 2 to 8. It serves as a forum in which the pupils have the chance to influence how the school is run, from the menus at lunchtime to helping the school to be more environmentally friendly.
The Council meets on a weekly basis and the elected members change each term giving everyone a chance to take part and have their voice heard.
Health
The health and wellbeing of our children is paramount at Broomwood. Our qualified nurses and school Matrons are on hand to support all our pupils’ needs and requirements.
On admission, we ask for a thorough medical history and to be kept updated should any changes occur. If a child needs regular prescribed medication, with parental authorisation, this can be done via staff at school. The school medical team is also able to provide medication such as mild pain killers (e.g., Calpol) with parental permission.
On a day-to-day basis, it is also important that parents let the school secretary or nurse know if children have had any medication prior to coming to school.
Parents will be contacted if we feel that pupils are too unwell to remain in school or if an injury needs further medical attention.
Find out more

Community & Sustainability
Community & Sustainability
Teaching our children about the importance of caring for our planet and using its resources sustainably is an integral part of a Broomwood education. We encourage all our young people to think beyond their own experiences and to reflect on how their actions might impact others. Being part of the wider community comes with responsibilities, and whether they are working on an initiative to reduce waste, or raising money for a good cause we want to produce young people who are tolerant and empathetic.

Governance
‘The Green Team ‘
Children at each of our sites form part of an Eco Group. They discuss ways in which the school can be more environmentally aware, from litter picking to recycling old school uniform and walking or cycling to school, instead of going by car. As well as encouraging children to connect with nature through our gardening clubs and outdoor learning (& younger pupil ‘welly time’) we also have a ‘living roof’ on the top of our pre-prep hall.
The Importance of Charitable Giving
Philanthropy is an integral and important part of a Broomwood education. The experience of raising money for charity brings big benefits to both recipients and participants.
Children learn about worlds beyond their own experience. They also learn fundraising and entrepreneurial skills, tolerance and empathy, and discover, just by small acts of giving, how to effect change, the multiplier effect of small acts and the large impact that their help can make on the lives of others.
A Proud History
Broomwood has a record of charitable fundraising and over the past 30 years has raised over £1m for numerous charities. The funds come from a myriad of different activities including colour fun runs, cake, book and uniform sales, own clothes and crazy hair days as well as sponsored activities and individual efforts from families and children.

Curriculum
A Broad Education
At Broomwood, we follow the National Curriculum yet pride ourselves in offering a broad range of additional academic study, stretching far beyond the classroom. We place a great emphasis on helping children to develop skills of enquiry, harnessing their natural curiosity and helping them make connections between subjects under broad themes. Boys and girls regularly go on visits, tours, and – for our older children – residential field trips. We also host a huge variety of events, from junior workshops to visiting speakers, specialist sports training, debating and poetry evenings, and concerts.
Our class sizes are small so we can provide the right levels of support, enrichment and challenge tailored to suit the needs of each pupil. We are not a ‘one size fits all’ school and we continually monitor progress and give regular feedback to parents.
English
‘Reading matters at Broomwood’
At Broomwood, we believe language is the key to understanding, expression, and imagination.
From their very first steps in education, we nurture a love of reading and writing, guiding your child to explore worlds beyond their own, whilst also building the lifelong skills of effective communication.
However, English doesn’t just sit behind a desk. We provide a tapestry of enriching experiences: Inter-House Competitions, rigorous debates, external competitions, and author visits. Every child’s journey is as unique as their voice, and we tailor our support to their individual needs, ensuring that they grow into articulate, thoughtful communicators – confident, precise, and ever-curious.
We can’t wait to talk more with you about what makes Broomwood such a special place to inspire a lifelong love of the written word in your children.
From the first day at Broomwood Pre-Prep, we start learning phonics, encompassing reading, writing, handwriting and spelling. By the end of Reception, all our children will have begun to master these skills. Each class has its own books and reading corner and our well-stocked libraries allow children to explore a wide range of reading material. We encourage them to enjoy all genres, including non-fiction, fiction or poetry. All children may borrow books to take home.
It is vital that your child has a good command of English so that they can access the full curriculum as they move through Broomwood. Our pupils practise the reading and writing skills they have learnt, whilst studying topics in our Thematic Learning programme and we are proud of the standard they reach.
At Broomwood Boys, we ignite a passion for English that will transcend their time at our school.
Our curriculum has been designed to prepare your son for his examinations, but we are proud to say that we maintain fun and excitement in all that we do.
With us, your son will go from reading Roald Dahl, Katherine Rundell and Joseph Coelho to Malorie Blackman, George Orwell and William Shakespeare. We don’t shy away from the classics. It is our belief that engaging with books head-on, supporting each boy to reach their fullest potential, empowers your son to embrace the challenge and complexity and to be a lifelong lover of literature. We are assisted in this drive by our well-stocked and up to date library, from which your son can borrow book a book whenever he wants. And, if he wants to read something we don’t currently have, he need only ask and it will be in his hands in no time.
Examinations are a part of English, but we prepare boys so that they are ready far before they are taking their seats in the examination room. It is what we do. Our students have earned scholarships and exhibitions from some of Britain’s finest and most prestigious schools including Winchester, Dulwich, Trinity and Whitgift.
Beyond the classroom, your son will have the opportunity to engage in amazing opportunities. Boys participate in writing and poetry competitions, debates, and inter-school events like the Bradfield Demosthenes competition, where our pupils recently triumphed. Not to mention, the inspirational visitors: from war correspondents to bestselling authors – we are inspired by their creativity, and it fuels our own literary passion.
At Broomwood, we speak passionately because we are passionate about what we do. We believe your son has the potential to become an articulate and erudite communicator, and we are committed to guiding him every step of the way on this transformative journey.
We have a busy and exciting English programme at Broomwood Prep – Girls and our goal is to instil a lifelong love of literature and language. On a practical level, we aim to empower girls to communicate effectively in speech and writing, with a secure understanding of spelling, punctuation and grammar.
The English teachers at Broomwood are passionate about their subject and have a wealth of experience. This ensures that pupils are well-prepared for any external exam required for entry to their chosen senior school. iPads enhance the teaching of English and are used in lessons for research purposes and vocabulary work, and for sharing and discussing pupils’ work.
Girls study prose, poetry and non-fiction from a range of cultures and periods of history. This provides ample opportunities to deepen the pupils’ understanding of the world. In addition, cross-curricular links, such as teaching Bali Rai’s ‘Mohinder’s War’ alongside a history unit of work on World War Two, teach the pupils how to form opinions and respond with sensitivity, enabling them to become perceptive, kind and tolerant young women.
Pre-Prep
Prep-Boys
Prep-Girls
Maths
We live in a world built on maths. It is the foundation of science, computing, finance – even music. Few subjects have been as important to the development of the society we live in today and the things we rely on and take for granted.
Our aim is for all pupils to leave Broomwood as confident and competent mathematicians. We believe that the best way to achieve this is to encourage resilience. We encourage pupils to take risks, to have a go and to be unafraid of make those essential mistakes that do so much to facilitate learning.
At Broomwood Pre-Prep, we use a mastery approach in maths, sometimes referred to as ‘Singaporean Maths’. This involves breaking down concepts into practical elements to ensure your child has a thorough understanding of each component. We have seen strong and continuing positive results and we are a training school for Maths Mastery. Most of our children cite maths as one of their favourite subjects.
We want your son to gain an understanding of ideas, logic and concepts, which he will be able to apply to his everyday life. We also know that many competitive senior schools are looking for students who are mathematically literate. We prepare boys to achieve at the highest level possible – and our exam results are a testament to that.
Your son will be encouraged to develop important mental skills like problem solving, logical thinking, effective communication of methods and answers, as well as imagination and the perception of shapes, objects and questions.
It is important to us that our boys achieve the grades of which they are capable; but we also want them to continue to explore and learn about maths and its role in the world around them and, most importantly of all, to enjoy their maths lessons.
Pupils at Broomwood Prep – Girls are taught maths in practical and relevant ways. We want your daughter to be able to investigate statements and communicate her thoughts clearly using accurate mathematical language. As soon as the foundation is in place, she can start to reach her own conclusions or come up with her own rules and patterns – this is where maths becomes incredibly rewarding and good fun.
Our teaching follows the highly effective mastery style which allows pupils to achieve fluency and depth in their learning, and to apply their skills and knowledge through reasoning and problem solving activities. We know these methods work and are proud of the results our girls achieve in the 11+, pre-test and 13+ examinations.
Pre-Prep
Prep-Boys
Prep-Girls
Science
In an age where we are bombarded with information from many sources, Science is an important discipline. At Broomwood, we aim to give your child the skills to think scientifically and to differentiate between fact and fiction. This develops a sense of the world and promotes the ability of our pupils to think for themselves.
We encourage children to see Science as relevant to their everyday life, and an essential part of their future. Learning through doing is at the very heart of the department’s Science teaching, and lessons are developed to promote curiosity, excitement and independent learning.
Children in the Pre-Prep study science within our thematic learning programme, exploring the subjects more formally in Year 3. In addition to lessons in the classroom, we take them on a variety of trips, including London Zoo, The Science Museum, The Natural History Museum and Kew Gardens.
Boys at Broomwood are taught Biology, Chemistry and Physics in fully equipped Science laboratories. Every year at Broomwood Boys, we also hold a competitive Science Fair in which the pupils present their scientific inventions and experiments. We invite guest Scientists to judge the work and the boys have been highly commended for the quality and creativity of their scientific research and ideas.
We supplement work at school by taking the boys to museums and exhibitions and liaising with senior schools for science days There is also an annual Geography and Science trip to the South of France.
We want every girl at Broomwood to be involved in Science and to learn how to use an investigative approach when conducting experiments. We have three modern and well-stocked laboratories. Science is taught by subject specialists who are passionate about what they do. From Year 7 onwards, girls have separate lessons in Physics, Chemistry and Biology as we prepare them for moving on the senior school
Pre-Prep
Prep-Boys
Prep-Girls
Languages
At Broomwood, we believe that learning languages builds confidence, cultural awareness, and strong communication skills. All pupils study French from Year 1, engaging in a variety of activities such as games, films, immersive trips, and cultural events to bring the language to life. Latin is introduced in later years, reinforcing linguistic understanding, enhancing analytical thinking, and providing insight into classical civilisation. Through the study of languages, children gain a broader perspective on the world and a deeper appreciation of different cultures and histories.
We teach Latin at Broomwood (Boys and Girls) from Year 6. Studying the Romans opens the pupils’ minds to the mechanics behind the language and also develops critical thinking skills required for the learning of modern languages. It also introduces our children to an exciting world of ancient history and mythology. From Julius Caesar to Odysseus via Cloelia, with many ghoulish monsters thrown in, the children revel in the stories and are encouraged to read more widely in English. The course takes a robust approach to grammar and vocabulary learning and we provide a range of engaging apps and games to support children with this. We want to spark a genuine interest in our pupils, giving them a confidence that will encourage them to study Classics at GCSE level and beyond.
At Broomwood Pre-Prep French is taught by a specialist teacher and the emphasis is on having fun! We follow a programme where children are encouraged to speak of everyday topics, through role play, drama and song. In these early years your child will be encouraged to absorb the sound of the language, get a taste for it and learn something of the enjoyable elements of French culture. This prepares them for moving on to Broomwood Prep, where they will study in more detail.
We want our children to have a thorough grounding in the basic structure of the languages they study. The languages we offer the boys, French and Latin complement and illuminate other subjects, such as English and History. We make use of the latest digital and technological advances in language teaching, including (for French) Quizlet and Linguascope.
Latin enhances pupils’ understanding of language structure, reinforcing English grammar and broadening vocabulary. Through classical texts and the study of Roman civilisation, pupils gain historical and cultural insights while developing logical thinking and problem-solving skills. Latin also provides a strong foundation for learning other languages, particularly those with Latin roots, and deepens pupils’ appreciation of the origins of modern language and literature.
The French curriculum is designed to foster a love for the French language and culture, while developing strong linguistic skills that will serve as a foundation for future learning. The French program encompasses the four skills: speaking, listening, reading, and writing, integrating both traditional language acquisition and interactive, real-world contexts to engage pupils.
Through our dynamic curriculum, students gain not only language skills but also a deeper appreciation for the rich cultural heritage of French-speaking countries. The aim is to instill a lifelong interest in languages and open doors to future educational and cultural opportunities. We also run an annual Year 6 residential trip to Normandy with Broomwood Girls.
The primary aim of the Modern Foreign Languages department at Broomwood Prep – Girls is to provide pupils with a thorough grounding in structure and grammar, as well as some experience of idiomatic use.
French is taught through speaking, listening, reading, and writing, with a strong emphasis on grammar, vocabulary, and cultural understanding. Extra Curricular
At Broomwood, we offer an extensive extra-curricular programme to complement and enhance our children’s timetabled lessons.
Extra-curricular clubs, activities, trips and workshops help develop our pupils’ ability to work side by side and build a sense of community.
One of the many ways we provide an inspiring and well-rounded education for our children is through a rich programme of trips and excursions.
From Little Broomwood and Pre-Prep to the Prep Boys and Prep Girls, all our pupils benefit from trips, tours and excursions. In the Pre-Prep, each year group goes on at least one excursion every year. Destinations have included Holly Lodge, Syon Park, The Horniman Museum, Chaulkney Meadows to the Museum of Childhood.
In the Prep School, excursions and longer co-educational residential trips play a vital part in broadening the experience we offer. All year groups have at least four one-day excursions each year, the purpose being to cover all the areas of the curriculum during a pupil’s time in the school.
Longer field trips assist in developing self-confidence – several trips are compulsory and others voluntary including a ski trip, hockey trip, choir and national sports tours.
Children benefit from different voices and different perspectives and to extend classroom boundaries, we organise several in-school workshops for pupils. These are delivered by specialists and help pupils to appreciate that subjects and topics are often interrelated. The workshops are often presented in a co-educational setting so that our Broomwood Prep – Boys and Broomwood Prep – girls learn alongside each other, and benefit from working together on extension projects.
The workshops complement our trips and excursions and are linked to topics being covered in the curriculum.

All Broomwood pupils benefit greatly from these hands-on educational experiences they take part in throughout the year.
We offer a wide range of after-school clubs at Broomwood, which vary across the year. Parents and children are notified about club options and book them at the start of each term.

Broomwood Pre – Prep (Year 1-3)
From Year 1 at Broomwood Pre-Prep, children may can stay after school to take part in diverse activities such as karate, chess, flamenco dancing, computer club, cricket, golf, ballet, dance, jewellery-making, art and crafts or cookery. The clubs programme changes every term and we encourage our children to have a go at a wide variety of different activities.
Clubs run from Monday-Thursday generally from 3.45-4.45. There is a charge – typically around £110 per term – but it can be a little more where higher costs are involved (for example external teachers or when travel is involved). The children are given tea at school before they start their clubs.
Broomwood Prep (Year 4-8)
In Broomwood Prep – Boys and Broomwood Prep – Girls there are endless options of after-school clubs, which also vary from term to term – some are exclusive to each school site and others are co-educational.
Clubs run after school Mondays to Thursdays from 5.20 to 6 or 6.20pm. There are also some lunch time clubs including Coding, Touch Typing, Choirs, Maths Surgery & Digital Art.

Junior Scholarship Programme
Broomwood is delighted to offer a Junior Scholarship Programme to pupils who demonstrate outstanding potential.
The ideal applicant will be a child who shows exceptional ability in an area of school life, alongside a strong academic aptitude. Chosen areas could include academics, drama, art, sport, or music.
Scholarships are available to suitable external and internal, from Broomwood Pre-Prep, applicants who are currently in Year 2 and moving into Year 3. External candidates may also apply for occasional places moving into Year 4.
Applications are currently closed and will reopen in the summer for September 2027 entry.
Assessments take place in March.
Please contact admissions@broomwood.com for more information.
